project_description: GitHub Copilot Agent Test Repository - EComApp multi-agent AI code analysis system with 12 specialized analysis agents

application_summary.purpose: A GitHub Copilot agent test repository that provides a complete multi-agent AI orchestration system for comprehensive source code analysis of an ECommerce application (EComApp). The system coordinates 12 specialized AI agents to deliver documentation generation, quality assessment, UML diagrams, BPMN process models, database schemas, architecture diagrams, and executive summaries.
key_functionalities: Automated GitHub issue assignment to Copilot via label-triggered workflow
Orchestrated multi-agent code analysis pipeline with 10 specialized agents
Source code documentation and business logic extraction (analysis_results.json, business_rules_extractor_analysis.json)
Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) generation and structural analysis
Code quality assessment with complexity metrics and technical debt identification
UML diagram generation (Class, Sequence, Use Case) in Mermaid format
BPMN 2.0 business process modeling with Mermaid flowcharts
Cloud and component architecture diagram generation
SQL DDL database schema generation from workflow analysis
Existing documentation quality analysis and comparison with code
Executive-level summary generation with strategic recommendations
technical_stack: Python diagrams library (architecture diagram code generation)
architecture_patterns: Multi-agent orchestration pattern with a central coordinator (orchestrator)
Pipeline pattern for sequential agent execution with dependency management
Parallel execution pattern (ast-analyzer can run concurrently with code-documentor)
Synthesis pattern where arc42-documentor aggregates all agent outputs
Analysis-only read-only pattern (no agent modifies source code)
Incremental output generation pattern (step-by-step file creation)
main_business_domains: Code Documentation and Business Logic Extraction
Software Quality Assessment and Technical Debt Management

.github/agents.description: AI agent specification definitions in Markdown format with YAML frontmatter. Each file defines a specialized agent with its name, description, tools, responsibilities, input/output contracts, and operational rules.

.github/workflows.description: GitHub Actions CI/CD workflow definitions. Contains the Copilot issue assignment automation workflow.

.github/hooks.description: Git hook placeholder directory. Contains an empty .keep file to maintain directory structure in version control.

.github/skills.description: GitHub Copilot skills placeholder directory. Contains an empty .keep file to maintain directory structure in version control.

files.summary: Minimal project description file that identifies the repository as the gs_test GitHub Copilot agent test repository.
files.description: The README.md serves as the entry point for the gs_test repository, providing only the project name and a single descriptive tagline. It identifies the project as a GitHub Copilot agent test repository but provides no installation, usage, architecture, or contribution documentation. The minimal content reflects the early stage or intentionally sparse nature of this test repository.

files.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that automatically assigns GitHub issues to GitHub Copilot when labeled with 'copilot-needed'.
files.description: This CI/CD workflow automates the delegation of GitHub issues to GitHub Copilot for AI-assisted resolution. It listens for issue labeling events and triggers when the 'copilot-needed' label is applied. The workflow uses a third-party action (otto-de/assign_issue_toCopilot_action) to perform the actual assignment using the repository's GitHub token for authentication. This enables seamless integration between issue tracking and AI-powered development assistance.
business_rules: Issues labeled with 'copilot-needed' must be automatically assigned to GitHub Copilot
The workflow triggers exclusively on issue labeling events (not on issue creation or other events)
Authentication must use the GITHUB_TOKEN secret from repository secrets
The assignment action version must be pinned to v1.0.1 for stability

method_breakdown.summary: Evaluates if the triggering issue contains the 'copilot-needed' label and if so invokes the Copilot assignment action
parameters: github.event.issue.labels (array): Labels on the triggering issue
method_breakdown.returns: Assigns the GitHub issue to GitHub Copilot
method_breakdown.significance: Core automation that bridges issue tracking with AI-assisted development, enabling GitHub Copilot to automatically pick up and process labeled issues

files.summary: Master coordinator agent specification that manages and sequences 10 specialized analysis agents for comprehensive, multi-faceted source code analysis.
files.description: The orchestrator agent acts as the central intelligence for coordinating a complete code analysis pipeline. It determines which agents are needed for a given analysis request, enforces execution order and dependency rules between agents, and delegates final documentation synthesis to the arc42-documentor. The orchestrator supports both full-pipeline execution and targeted analysis for specific requests (e.g., UML only, quality only). It communicates progress updates to users and maintains systematic, transparent operation. The orchestrator itself does not perform analysis but instead coordinates specialized agents and synthesizes their communication.
business_rules: code-documentor must always execute first as the foundational data provider for all other agents
ast-analyzer may execute in parallel with code-documentor
code-assessor requires code-documentor output before it can run
uml-generator requires outputs from both code-documentor and ast-analyzer
bpmn-generator requires code-documentor output before it can run
ddl-generator requires workflow analysis output from code-documentor
architecture-analyzer requires outputs from all preceding agents
documentation-analyzer analyzes existing docs and compares against code analysis outputs
executive-summary must run after all technical analysis agents and before arc42-documentor
arc42-documentor must always run as the final synthesis step
No source code files may be modified by any orchestrated agent
No code execution or test running is permitted by any agent
Analysis must proceed file-by-file in a deterministic, consistent order
Input folder path and output folder path must be provided by the user
Targeted analysis selects only relevant agents based on request type
The orchestrator must provide progress updates during long-running analyses
Errors in one agent must not halt execution of other independent agents

method_breakdown.summary: Identifies which analysis modules are needed based on user request and determines full vs. targeted analysis scope
parameters: user_request (string): Natural language description of desired analysis
method_breakdown.returns: Analysis plan specifying which agents to execute
method_breakdown.significance: Critical first step that determines the scope and efficiency of the entire analysis pipeline

method_breakdown.summary: Determines execution order respecting inter-agent dependencies and identifying opportunities for parallel execution
method_breakdown.returns: Ordered execution plan with dependency annotations
method_breakdown.significance: Ensures correct sequencing and optimal parallelization of the analysis pipeline

method_breakdown.summary: Invokes specialized agents in the planned sequence using the runSubagent tool, communicating status to users at each step
parameters: execution_plan (list): Ordered list of agents to invoke
input_path (string): Source code input folder path
method_breakdown.returns: Aggregated analysis outputs from all invoked agents
method_breakdown.significance: Core orchestration function that drives the multi-agent analysis pipeline

method_breakdown.summary: Calls the arc42-documentor agent as the final step to synthesize all agent outputs into comprehensive Arc42 architecture documentation
parameters: all_agent_outputs (object): Collected outputs from all preceding agents
method_breakdown.returns: ARC42_DOCUMENTATION.md - complete self-contained architecture document
method_breakdown.significance: Produces the final deliverable that integrates all analysis perspectives into a single authoritative document

files.summary: Comprehensive combined analysis agent that integrates all 10 specialized agent capabilities into a single unified workflow for complete code analysis.
files.description: The all-in-one-code-analyzer provides the complete analysis pipeline as a single agent, combining documentation extraction, quality assessment, AST generation, UML/BPMN diagram creation, architecture visualization, database schema generation, documentation analysis, executive summarization, and Arc42 documentation synthesis. This agent is an alternative to using the orchestrator with separate agents, providing the same functionality in a single coordinated execution. It supports both full analysis and targeted module selection based on user requests. All outputs are organized in the same structured folder hierarchy as the individual agents use.
business_rules: Code documentation must always be the first step in full analysis execution
AST generation can execute in parallel with code documentation
All diagrams must use Mermaid format exclusively (no PlantUML, no ASCII art)
Source code files must never be modified
Code must never be executed or tested
Output files must be organized in analysis_output/ with agent-specific subdirectories
All file creation and modification must be logged to analysis_output/agent-log.txt
Processing must be deterministic and file-by-file
Every issue identified must have an actionable recommendation
Arc42 documentation must be completely self-contained with embedded Mermaid diagrams
No external file references are allowed in Arc42 documentation
If analysis is interrupted, resume from last checkpoint
If a file is too large, process in chunks
technical_libraries: Python diagrams library (for architecture diagram code generation)

method_breakdown.method_name: Code Documentation and Business Logic Extraction
method_breakdown.summary: Analyzes source code files to extract business rules, workflows, domain logic and generates analysis_results.json and business_rules_extractor_analysis.json
method_breakdown.returns: analysis_results.json, business_rules_extractor_analysis.json, package_summary.json, application_summary.json
method_breakdown.significance: Foundational step that all other analysis modules depend upon

method_breakdown.method_name: Quality Assessment and Technical Debt Analysis
method_breakdown.summary: Evaluates code quality on a 0-10 scale, identifies issues with 1-5 criticality ratings, documents technical debt, and provides enhancement recommendations
method_breakdown.returns: assessment_summary.json, COMPREHENSIVE_ASSESSMENT_REPORT.md
method_breakdown.significance: Identifies actionable improvements and quantifies technical debt for prioritization

method_breakdown.summary: Creates detailed JSON representations of Abstract Syntax Trees capturing classes, methods, statements, control flow, and dependencies
method_breakdown.returns: [ClassName]_AST.json files per source file, AST_Analysis_Summary.md
method_breakdown.significance: Provides deep structural analysis used by UML generator, BPMN generator, and other downstream agents

method_breakdown.summary: Generates Class, Sequence, and Use Case diagrams in Mermaid format from code structure analysis
method_breakdown.returns: class-diagram.md, sequence-diagram.md, use-case-diagram.md with embedded Mermaid code
method_breakdown.significance: Provides visual representation of system structure and behavior for stakeholder communication

method_breakdown.summary: Translates business workflows and code logic into Mermaid flowchart diagrams representing business processes
method_breakdown.returns: BPMN Markdown files with embedded Mermaid flowcharts
method_breakdown.significance: Bridges technical implementation and business process documentation for stakeholder alignment

method_breakdown.summary: Creates cloud architecture diagrams (AWS/Azure/GCP) and component architecture diagrams in Mermaid format
parameters: all_previous_outputs (object): Combined outputs from all preceding steps
method_breakdown.returns: ARCHITECTURE_SUMMARY.md with embedded Mermaid architecture diagrams
method_breakdown.significance: Communicates infrastructure and deployment architecture to technical and business stakeholders

method_breakdown.summary: Generates optimized SQL DDL files from workflow analysis and field documentation for multiple database dialects
method_breakdown.returns: schema.sql, schema_summary.json, database schema Markdown documentation
method_breakdown.significance: Provides database schema definitions ready for review and deployment

method_breakdown.summary: Analyzes existing project documentation for quality, completeness, accuracy, and alignment with code implementation
method_breakdown.returns: DOCUMENTATION_QUALITY_REPORT.md, documentation_analysis.json, comparison_report.json
method_breakdown.significance: Identifies documentation gaps and discrepancies that could mislead developers

method_breakdown.summary: Synthesizes all technical findings into executive-level insights with strengths, weaknesses, strategic recommendations, and action plans
parameters: all_technical_outputs (object): Combined outputs from all preceding analysis steps
method_breakdown.returns: EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md with prioritized recommendations and metrics dashboard
method_breakdown.significance: Translates technical findings into business-relevant insights for decision-makers

method_breakdown.summary: Synthesizes all analysis outputs into a comprehensive, self-contained Arc42 architecture documentation with embedded Mermaid diagrams
parameters: all_agent_outputs (object): Complete outputs from all preceding agents including executive summary
method_breakdown.returns: ARC42_DOCUMENTATION.md - complete self-contained architecture document with 12 sections
method_breakdown.significance: Produces the definitive architectural reference document integrating all analysis perspectives

files.summary: Specialized agent for synthesizing outputs from all analysis agents into a comprehensive, self-contained Arc42 architecture documentation with embedded Mermaid diagrams.
files.description: The arc42-documentor agent serves as the final synthesis step in the analysis pipeline, consuming outputs from all 8 preceding specialized agents and assembling them into a complete Arc42 architecture documentation. It generates all 12 Arc42 sections incrementally to avoid token/context limit issues, embedding all diagram code directly in the Markdown document. The agent enforces strict self-containment (no external file references) and uses only Mermaid syntax for all diagrams. It is always the last agent to run in any full analysis workflow.
business_rules: arc42-documentor must always be the final agent executed in any full analysis workflow
All diagrams must use Mermaid format exclusively (never PlantUML or ASCII art)
The final document must be completely self-contained with no external file references
All Mermaid diagram code must be embedded directly in ARC42_DOCUMENTATION.md
Documentation must be generated incrementally one section at a time to avoid token limits
Sections must be generated in order from 1 (Introduction) through 12 (Glossary)
If input data is missing, use placeholder text '[Information not available from analysis]'
Missing data must be noted with suggestions for which agent to re-run
All content must be based on actual analysis results, not assumptions
Architecture documentation must cover all 12 Arc42 sections
Output must be saved to ARC42_DOCUMENTATION.md
Output must be encoded in UTF-8
All outputs must be logged to analysis_output/agent-log.txt

method_breakdown.summary: Lists available analysis outputs, maps them to Arc42 sections, and saves an execution plan
parameters: workspace_outputs (list): All available analysis output files from preceding agents
method_breakdown.returns: Execution plan mapping analysis files to Arc42 sections
method_breakdown.significance: Ensures systematic coverage of all 12 Arc42 sections with available data

method_breakdown.summary: Creates ARC42_DOCUMENTATION.md with header and table of contents as the initial scaffold
method_breakdown.returns: ARC42_DOCUMENTATION.md with header and 12-section table of contents
method_breakdown.significance: Establishes the document structure before incremental content addition

method_breakdown.summary: Generates each of the 12 Arc42 sections sequentially, reading relevant inputs, embedding diagrams, and appending to the document
parameters: relevant_inputs (object): Analysis outputs relevant to current section
method_breakdown.returns: Section content appended to ARC42_DOCUMENTATION.md with embedded Mermaid diagrams
method_breakdown.significance: Core generation loop that produces all 12 sections of the final architecture document

method_breakdown.summary: Reviews the complete document, verifies all diagrams are embedded (no external references), and confirms self-containment
method_breakdown.returns: Validated, self-contained ARC42_DOCUMENTATION.md
method_breakdown.significance: Ensures the final document is complete, consistent, and fully self-contained

files.summary: Specialized agent for generating cloud and component architecture diagrams in Mermaid format by analyzing application structure, dependencies, and technology stack.
files.description: The architecture-analyzer agent produces two types of architecture diagrams: cloud infrastructure diagrams (mapping application components to cloud services on AWS, Azure, or GCP) and component architecture diagrams (showing internal application structure). It reads code analysis outputs from all preceding agents to understand the technology stack, architecture patterns, and component relationships. The agent generates Mermaid diagrams as well as Python diagrams library code for higher-fidelity PNG rendering. It also provides cloud migration recommendations based on detected technologies and provides JSON metadata about the architecture.
business_rules: All diagrams must use Mermaid format exclusively (never PlantUML or ASCII art)
Cloud architecture diagrams must map application components to appropriate cloud services
Component architecture diagrams must show all application layers (frontend, backend, data, integration)
Architecture must be detected from code analysis results, not assumed
Architecture best practices must be documented (scalability, HA, security, performance, cost, observability)
Migration recommendations must be categorized (Compute, Database, Storage, Caching, Monitoring)
Each migration recommendation must include benefit and effort assessment
The agent must not deploy infrastructure or modify source code
Graphviz must be installed for PNG rendering (documented as requirement)
Architecture diagrams output is consumed by arc42-documentor for final documentation

method_breakdown.summary: Reads application summary, package structure, dependencies, and business capabilities from all preceding agent outputs
parameters: all_agent_outputs (object): Combined outputs from code-documentor, ast-analyzer, code-assessor, uml-generator, bpmn-generator, ddl-generator
method_breakdown.returns: Extracted technology stack, architecture patterns, and component information
method_breakdown.significance: Grounds architecture diagrams in actual code analysis rather than assumptions

method_breakdown.summary: Detects the architectural pattern (Monolithic, Layered, Microservices, Event-Driven, Serverless) from code structure
method_breakdown.returns: Detected architecture pattern with confidence level
method_breakdown.significance: Determines the type of architecture diagram to generate

method_breakdown.summary: Translates detected application components to equivalent cloud services for AWS, Azure, or GCP
method_breakdown.returns: Component-to-cloud-service mapping for diagram generation
method_breakdown.significance: Bridges application architecture to cloud deployment recommendations

method_breakdown.summary: Produces Mermaid cloud architecture diagram and Python diagrams library code for the detected/target cloud provider
method_breakdown.returns: Mermaid diagram code and Python diagrams code in JSON format with metadata
method_breakdown.significance: Primary deliverable showing infrastructure deployment topology

method_breakdown.summary: Produces Mermaid component diagram showing application layers and internal component relationships
method_breakdown.returns: Mermaid component architecture diagram in Markdown format
method_breakdown.significance: Shows internal application structure for developer communication

method_breakdown.summary: Produces categorized cloud migration recommendations with benefits and effort estimates based on code analysis
method_breakdown.returns: JSON array of migration recommendations categorized by area
method_breakdown.significance: Provides actionable cloud adoption guidance grounded in code analysis

files.summary: Specialized agent for generating detailed Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) JSON representations from source code, capturing complete structural analysis of classes, methods, statements, control flow, and dependencies.
files.description: The ast-analyzer agent parses source code files and produces structured JSON AST representations that capture all code elements: type declarations, method definitions with complete logic flow, control flow structures, variable declarations, and import dependencies. It supports any programming language and adapts its analysis approach accordingly. The AST output is used by downstream agents (uml-generator, bpmn-generator, code-documentor) for structural analysis and diagram generation. The agent can work independently from source code or leverage code-documentor outputs for enriched context.
business_rules: AST must include complete representation of all structural elements (classes, interfaces, enums, methods, fields)
All statement types must be captured: conditionals, loops, try-catch, assignments, method invocations, return statements
Return statements must always include a 'value' field (null if no return value)
Exact type information must be preserved in the AST
All annotations/decorators must be documented with their parameters
Generic type parameters and bounds must be captured
Nested structures (inner classes, anonymous classes, closures) must be properly represented
Source code files must never be modified
Code must never be executed or interpreted
AST files must be output as valid JSON parsable by Python's json.loads()
One AST JSON file must be generated per source code file
All outputs must be written to analysis_output/ast-analyzer/

method_breakdown.summary: Extracts all class, interface, enum, and struct declarations with their modifiers, parent types, and implemented interfaces
method_breakdown.returns: Array of TypeDeclaration objects with name, modifiers, annotations, parent, interfaces
method_breakdown.significance: Foundation of the AST representing the top-level type structure of each file

method_breakdown.summary: Extracts all method and function definitions including modifiers, return types, parameters, annotations, Javadoc, and complete body statement sequences
parameters: type_declaration (object): Parent type containing the method
method_breakdown.returns: Array of MethodDeclaration objects with complete body statement AST
method_breakdown.significance: Most critical AST component used by BPMN generator for workflow extraction and UML generator for sequence diagrams

method_breakdown.summary: Extracts if/else, switch, while, for, do-while, and try-catch-finally statements with their conditions, bodies, and branches
parameters: statement_node (object): Statement node from the parse tree
method_breakdown.returns: Typed statement objects (IfStatement, WhileStatement, TryStatement, etc.) with condition and body
method_breakdown.significance: Enables business process extraction and complexity calculation by capturing all decision points and loops

method_breakdown.summary: Extracts class and instance field declarations with their types, modifiers, initial values, and annotations
parameters: type_declaration (object): Parent type containing the field
method_breakdown.returns: Array of FieldDeclaration objects with name, type, modifiers, value, annotations
method_breakdown.significance: Provides data structure information for DDL generation and class diagram creation

method_breakdown.summary: Extracts all import statements, include directives, and using statements representing external dependencies
method_breakdown.returns: Array of import/dependency strings
method_breakdown.significance: Provides dependency information for architecture analysis and component relationship diagrams

files.summary: Specialized BPMN process modeling agent that translates source code workflows, business rules, and control flow logic into Mermaid flowchart diagrams representing business processes.
files.description: The bpmn-generator agent creates visual representations of business processes extracted from source code analysis. It maps code constructs (if-else → decision gateways, loops → loop tasks, try-catch → error paths, method chains → sequence flows) to BPMN 2.0 elements represented as Mermaid flowcharts. The agent uses business rules from code-documentor and AST control flow from ast-analyzer as inputs. It supports BPMN patterns including orchestration, choreography, saga, and event-driven processes. All output diagrams use Mermaid syntax exclusively and are embedded in Markdown documentation files.
business_rules: All BPMN diagrams must use Mermaid flowchart syntax exclusively (never BPMN XML, PlantUML, or ASCII art)
Every process flow must have clearly labeled start and end events
All gateway outgoing flows must be labeled with their conditions
Error handling paths must be included for processes with exception handling
Swimlanes must be used to show participant responsibilities
Business terminology must be used in node labels (not technical jargon)
BPMN diagrams must represent business processes, not implementation details
Every code path must eventually reach an end event
Process elements must include: start events, end events, tasks, gateways, flows
Process metadata (participants, error types, element counts) must be documented
Source code must never be modified
Output must be written to analysis_output/bpmn-generator/

method_breakdown.summary: Reads business rules from code-documentor and AST control flow from ast-analyzer to identify process boundaries and workflow steps
method_breakdown.returns: Process definitions with steps, decisions, and participants
method_breakdown.significance: Grounds BPMN diagrams in actual code-extracted business logic

method_breakdown.summary: Identifies entry points (controllers, API endpoints), exit points (return statements, final states), and external system interactions
method_breakdown.returns: Process boundary definitions with start/end events and external interactions
method_breakdown.significance: Determines the scope of each BPMN process model

method_breakdown.method_name: Map Code Constructs to BPMN Elements
method_breakdown.summary: Translates code constructs to BPMN elements: methods→tasks, conditionals→gateways, loops→loop tasks, exceptions→error events
parameters: ast_nodes (list): AST statement nodes to translate
method_breakdown.returns: BPMN element definitions ready for Mermaid rendering
method_breakdown.significance: Core translation function that bridges code logic and business process notation

method_breakdown.summary: Creates swimlane definitions based on user roles, external systems, and internal services identified in the code
parameters: participants (list): Identified process participants from code analysis
method_breakdown.returns: Swimlane structure as Mermaid subgraphs
method_breakdown.significance: Improves diagram readability by organizing responsibilities by participant

method_breakdown.summary: Produces final Mermaid flowchart code with proper styling for start/end events, gateways, and tasks, along with JSON metadata
method_breakdown.returns: JSON with Mermaid code, metadata (element counts, participants, error types), and Markdown documentation file
method_breakdown.significance: Primary deliverable for business process visualization

files.summary: Specialized code quality assessment agent that evaluates complexity, identifies issues with severity ratings, documents technical debt, and provides detailed, actionable enhancement recommendations.
files.description: The code-assessor agent performs comprehensive quality evaluation of source code using a standardized assessment framework. It rates code complexity and logic complexity on 0-10 scales, identifies issues categorized by type (security, performance, maintainability, etc.) with 1-5 criticality ratings, documents technical debt by category (code, design, test, documentation, infrastructure), and recommends enhancements with priority ratings and code examples. All solutions provided must be specific to the exact code being assessed, not generic. The agent leverages code-documentor and ast-analyzer outputs for enriched analysis context.
business_rules: Code complexity must be rated on a 0-10 scale (0-2 very simple, 9-10 very complex)
Logic complexity must be rated on a 0-10 scale separate from code complexity
Every detected issue must have: line number, issue type, message, criticality (1-5), specific solution, and estimated time
Issue solutions must be specific to the exact code being assessed (not generic advice)
Issue solution descriptions must explain HOW to fix it and WHAT benefits it brings
Issue solutions should include code examples where applicable
Issue criticality 5 (Blocker) is reserved for security vulnerabilities, data corruption, system crashes
Issue criticality 4 (Severe) covers performance bottlenecks, memory leaks, data integrity issues
Issue criticality 3 (Normal) covers maintainability issues, missing error handling, inefficient algorithms
Issue criticality 2 (Minor) covers naming inconsistencies and minor readability issues
Issue criticality 1 (Trivial) covers formatting and style preferences
At least three enhancement recommendations must be provided per file
Enhancement priorities must be rated 1-5 with code examples
Technical debt must be categorized: Code, Design, Test, Documentation, Infrastructure
Technical debt items must have: type, description, impact (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), estimated fix time
Source code files must never be modified
Output must be written to analysis_output/code-assessor/
files.sub_capability: Quality Assessment and Technical Debt Analysis

method_breakdown.summary: Rates code complexity (readability) and logic complexity (business logic difficulty) on independent 0-10 scales
method_breakdown.returns: code_complexity (int 0-10), logic_complexity (int 0-10)
method_breakdown.significance: Provides quantifiable metrics for code maintainability and cognitive load assessment

method_breakdown.summary: Identifies code issues by type (security, performance, maintainability, etc.) with line-level location and 1-5 criticality ratings
method_breakdown.returns: Array of Issue objects with line number, type, message, criticality, solution, and estimated time
method_breakdown.significance: Core output for development team prioritization and sprint planning

method_breakdown.summary: Generates at least three enhancement recommendations with detailed descriptions, code examples, and priority ratings
parameters: issues (list): Detected issues from Issue Detection
method_breakdown.returns: Array of Enhancement objects with title, description, code example, and priority (1-5)
method_breakdown.significance: Provides actionable improvement roadmap for development teams

method_breakdown.summary: Documents technical debt items categorized by type with impact assessment and estimated resolution time
method_breakdown.returns: Array of TechnicalDebt objects with type, description, impact (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), and estimated fix time
method_breakdown.significance: Quantifies accumulated technical debt for management reporting and remediation planning

files.summary: Foundational code documentation agent that analyzes source code files and generates analysis_results.json and business_rules_extractor_analysis.json as the primary inputs for all other analysis agents.
files.description: The code-documentor agent is the first and most critical agent in the analysis pipeline, responsible for extracting business logic, classifying files, documenting code structure, and producing structured JSON outputs. It analyzes each source file systematically to produce summaries, categories, business rules, method breakdowns, and business capabilities. The agent also generates application summaries, package-wise summaries, configuration analyses, business rules extractions, one-pager summaries, persona analyses, and field analyses. It works independently without dependencies on other agents and serves as the foundation that all other agents build upon.
business_rules: code-documentor must always be the first agent executed in the analysis pipeline
Every source code file must be classified as Business, Technical, or Mixed
File descriptions must focus on business responsibility (3-5 sentences) excluding technical implementation details
Business rules must be extracted as a list for each file
Method breakdown must document: method_name, summary, parameters, returns, dependencies, significance
Technical libraries must exclude standard library components
Output JSON must be parsable by Python's json.loads()
JSON output must use single-line strings with no escape characters or line breaks
No code block markers (json) are allowed in JSON output files
The first log entry must be 'I am a penguin'
All outputs must be written to analysis_output/code-documentor/
All file creation must be logged to analysis_output/agent-log.txt
Source code files must never be modified
Code must never be executed or tested
Test files must be used to enrich business rule extraction when available
Files must be processed in a consistent, deterministic order
files.sub_capability: Business Logic Extraction and Structural Documentation

method_breakdown.summary: Categorizes each source file as Business (domain logic), Technical (infrastructure/data access), or Mixed (both)
method_breakdown.returns: Category string: 'Business' | 'Technical' | 'Mixed'
method_breakdown.significance: Enables filtered analysis and helps stakeholders understand code composition

method_breakdown.summary: Extracts summary, description, business rules, technical libraries, business capability, and sub-capability from each source file
method_breakdown.returns: File analysis object with all core elements
method_breakdown.significance: Primary data extraction that feeds all downstream analysis agents

method_breakdown.summary: Analyzes each method/function to document name, summary, parameters, returns, dependencies, and significance
parameters: method_nodes (list): Method AST nodes from file
method_breakdown.returns: Array of method_breakdown objects
method_breakdown.significance: Provides granular method-level documentation used by UML generator and API documentation tools

method_breakdown.summary: Generates high-level application overview including purpose, key functionalities, technical stack, architecture patterns, and main business domains
method_breakdown.returns: Application summary object written to application_summary.json
method_breakdown.significance: Provides the big-picture overview consumed by executive-summary and arc42-documentor agents

method_breakdown.summary: Creates hierarchical summaries of package/module structure with responsibilities, dependencies, and key classes
parameters: all_file_analyses (list): File analyses organized by package/directory
method_breakdown.returns: Package summary object written to package_summary.json
method_breakdown.significance: Enables architecture-level understanding of code organization

method_breakdown.summary: Focuses specifically on extracting validation rules, calculation logic, workflow steps, decision criteria, and business constraints
parameters: all_file_analyses (list): Complete file analysis results including test files
method_breakdown.returns: Business rules JSON written to business_rules_extractor_analysis.json
method_breakdown.significance: Critical output for BPMN generator, DDL generator, and compliance documentation

files.summary: Specialized database schema design agent that generates optimized SQL DDL statements from workflow analysis and field documentation produced by the code-documentor agent.
files.description: The ddl-generator agent translates application data models and business rules into production-ready SQL DDL scripts. It analyzes field usage patterns, entity relationships, and validation constraints from code analysis to produce table definitions, primary/foreign keys, indexes, and constraints. The agent supports multiple SQL dialects (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, SQL Server) and follows best practices for naming conventions, data type selection, normalization, and documentation. It also produces Mermaid entity-relationship diagrams and Markdown schema documentation as companion artifacts.
business_rules: All ER diagrams must use Mermaid erDiagram format exclusively
Table names must be in plural snake_case (users, order_items)
Column names must be in snake_case (user_id, first_name)
Index naming convention: idx_tablename_columnname
Foreign key naming convention: fk_tablename_referencedtable
Constraint naming convention: chk_tablename_description
DECIMAL must be used for monetary values (never FLOAT or DOUBLE for money)
TIMESTAMP must be used for date-time values
All primary keys must be explicitly defined
NOT NULL constraints must be applied where business rules require non-null values
CHECK constraints must enforce value validation rules from business logic
Foreign keys must enforce referential integrity with appropriate CASCADE rules
All foreign key columns must have corresponding indexes
Frequently queried columns must be indexed
Audit columns (created_at, updated_at) must be included where appropriate
Table and column comments must be added to document their purpose
Soft delete patterns (is_deleted, deleted_at) must be used instead of hard DELETE where appropriate
DDL must never be executed against a live database
Output must be written to analysis_output/ddl-generator/
files.sub_capability: SQL DDL Generation from Code Analysis

method_breakdown.summary: Identifies database entities from class names, database annotations (@Entity, @Table), repository patterns, and field groupings
method_breakdown.returns: List of entity definitions with names and contexts
method_breakdown.significance: Determines the table structure for the generated schema

method_breakdown.summary: Maps each field to a column definition with appropriate data type, nullability, default value, and length/precision constraints
parameters: entity_fields (list): Field definitions from code analysis
method_breakdown.returns: Column definitions with data types and constraints
method_breakdown.significance: Core DDL generation that translates code fields to database columns

method_breakdown.summary: Identifies primary keys (id fields, @Id annotations) and foreign keys (entity references, @ManyToOne relationships)
parameters: entity_definitions (list): Entity field and relationship analysis
method_breakdown.returns: Primary key and foreign key definitions
method_breakdown.significance: Establishes entity identity and referential integrity in the schema

method_breakdown.summary: Translates business validation rules to SQL constraints (NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK) from validation annotations and business logic
method_breakdown.returns: SQL constraint definitions
method_breakdown.significance: Enforces business rules at the database level for data integrity

method_breakdown.summary: Creates indexes for foreign keys, frequently queried fields, WHERE clause fields, ORDER BY fields, and composite query patterns
parameters: query_patterns (list): Detected query patterns from data access code
method_breakdown.returns: CREATE INDEX statements
method_breakdown.significance: Performance optimization that prevents N+1 query problems and slow table scans

method_breakdown.summary: Produces Mermaid erDiagram visualizing table relationships with cardinality notation
method_breakdown.returns: Mermaid erDiagram code embedded in Markdown
method_breakdown.significance: Visual documentation of the data model for stakeholder communication

files.summary: Specialized documentation quality analyst agent that evaluates existing project documentation for completeness, accuracy, and alignment with actual code implementation.
files.description: The documentation-analyzer agent performs two complementary analyses: a Documents Summary that scores existing documentation across eight quality dimensions (completeness, clarity, accuracy, structure, accessibility, maintainability, examples, consistency), and a Comparison Report that identifies discrepancies between documented and implemented functionality. It leverages outputs from all preceding analysis agents to perform ground-truth comparison. The agent identifies critical gaps (essential missing information), major gaps (important incomplete information), and minor gaps (nice-to-have improvements), providing prioritized recommendations for each.
business_rules: Documentation quality must be scored on 0-10 scales across eight dimensions
Overall documentation score must be an average of all dimension scores
Critical gaps are defined as missing essential information that prevents system understanding
Major gaps are defined as important but incomplete information that causes significant difficulty
Minor gaps are defined as nice-to-have information that improves but is not essential
API discrepancies must be categorized as: missing_in_docs or documented_but_not_implemented
Documented-but-not-implemented features must be flagged as critical discrepancies
Version mismatches in dependencies must be documented with severity assessment
Architecture discrepancies between documented and actual architecture must be flagged as critical
All recommendations must have priority (critical/high/medium/low) and estimated effort
Existing documentation files must never be modified
Source code files must never be modified
Analysis compares against ALL preceding agent outputs for ground-truth comparison
Output must be written to analysis_output/documentation-analyzer/

method_breakdown.summary: Evaluates all project documentation files across eight quality dimensions and produces overall and per-document scores
parameters: documentation_files (list): All project documentation files (README, API docs, etc.)
method_breakdown.returns: JSON with overall score, per-dimension scores, per-document analysis, and gap categorization
method_breakdown.significance: Provides quantified documentation quality baseline for improvement planning

method_breakdown.summary: Compares documented functionality against actual code implementation to identify discrepancies in APIs, configurations, dependencies, features, and architecture
method_breakdown.returns: JSON comparison report with discrepancy counts, API/config/dependency/feature comparisons, and prioritized recommendations
method_breakdown.significance: Identifies documentation drift that can mislead developers and users

method_breakdown.summary: Categorizes missing or inadequate documentation into critical, major, and minor gaps with impact assessment and recommendations
method_breakdown.returns: Categorized gap list with impact descriptions and specific recommendations
method_breakdown.significance: Prioritizes documentation improvements for maximum developer productivity impact

files.summary: Strategic synthesis agent that transforms all technical analysis outputs into concise executive-level insights with strengths, weaknesses, risk assessment, and a prioritized strategic action plan.
files.description: The executive-summary agent is the penultimate step in the analysis pipeline, consuming outputs from all eight technical analysis agents to produce business-focused strategic insights. It presents application purpose, technical health scores across multiple dimensions, identified strengths and categorized weaknesses (critical/high/medium priority), and a three-horizon action plan (immediate/1-3 months/3-12 months). The agent translates technical findings into business impact language accessible to non-technical decision-makers. The executive summary feeds directly into the arc42-documentor as strategic context for the final architecture document.
business_rules: Executive summary must run after all technical analysis agents and before arc42-documentor
Application overview must be written in clear, jargon-free language accessible to non-technical stakeholders
Technical health must be scored across all dimensions: Code Quality, Architecture, Security, Performance, Maintainability, Documentation, Test Coverage, Technical Debt
All statements about strengths and weaknesses must cite factual evidence from code analysis
Weaknesses must be categorized by severity: Critical (red), High Priority (orange), Medium Priority (yellow)
Critical weaknesses (security vulnerabilities, data integrity risks) must be listed under Immediate Actions
Immediate actions must target the next 1-2 week sprint
Short-term improvements must target the 1-3 month horizon
Long-term strategic initiatives must target the 3-12 month horizon
Every recommendation must specify issue, impact, action, effort, and responsible team
Executive summary must be 2-4 pages maximum
No diagrams should be included in the executive summary (text-focused output)
Risk assessment must include likelihood, impact, and mitigation strategy
Source code files must never be modified
Output must be saved as executive-summary.md in the output folder

method_breakdown.summary: Synthesizes 2-3 paragraph business-focused overview of application purpose, core functionality, target users, business value, and technology stack
parameters: all_analysis_outputs (object): Combined outputs from all preceding agents
method_breakdown.returns: Application overview section in Markdown (2-3 paragraphs, business language)
method_breakdown.significance: Sets business context for all subsequent findings, ensuring executive alignment

method_breakdown.summary: Identifies and documents 3-5 key positive aspects of the codebase with factual evidence and specific metrics from code analysis
method_breakdown.returns: Technical strengths list with evidence and metrics in Markdown
method_breakdown.significance: Provides balanced perspective and acknowledges areas of good practice

method_breakdown.summary: Identifies and categorizes 3-7 concerns by severity (Critical/High/Medium), citing specific findings from code analysis
method_breakdown.returns: Categorized weakness list with severity indicators and business impact in Markdown
method_breakdown.significance: Prioritizes improvement areas by business impact for executive decision-making

method_breakdown.summary: Produces a multi-dimensional health score table with numerical scores and visual status indicators for all quality dimensions
parameters: quality_metrics (object): Aggregated quality metrics from all analysis agents
method_breakdown.returns: Health score Markdown table with dimension scores (0-10) and status icons (green/yellow/orange/red)
method_breakdown.significance: Provides a dashboard-style at-a-glance quality overview for executive communication

method_breakdown.summary: Creates three-horizon action plan (immediate/short-term/long-term) with specific issues, impacts, actions, effort estimates, and responsible teams
method_breakdown.returns: Prioritized action plan in Markdown organized by time horizon
method_breakdown.significance: Translates analysis findings into actionable roadmap for investment and planning decisions

method_breakdown.summary: Documents key risks if recommendations are not followed, with likelihood, impact, and mitigation strategies
parameters: critical_issues (list): Critical and high priority issues
method_breakdown.returns: Risk assessment section in Markdown with categorized risks
method_breakdown.significance: Enables risk-based prioritization of remediation efforts

files.summary: Specialized UML diagram generation agent that creates Class, Sequence, and Use Case diagrams exclusively in Mermaid format from code structure and AST analysis.
files.description: The uml-generator agent produces three types of UML diagrams in Mermaid format: Class Diagrams showing static structure with attributes, methods, and relationships; Sequence Diagrams showing interaction flows and method call sequences; and Use Case Diagrams showing system functionality from a user perspective. The agent derives diagram content from code-documentor analysis results and ast-analyzer structural outputs. All diagrams use Mermaid syntax exclusively and are embedded in Markdown documentation files. The agent supports package-level diagrams, component diagrams, and detailed class diagrams for large codebases.
business_rules: All UML diagrams must use Mermaid format exclusively (never PlantUML or ASCII art)
Class diagrams must use the Mermaid classDiagram syntax
Sequence diagrams must use the Mermaid sequenceDiagram syntax
Use case diagrams must use Mermaid flowchart or graph syntax
Class diagrams must show all visibility modifiers (+, -, #, ~)
Class diagrams must include all relationship types (inheritance, implementation, association, aggregation, composition, dependency)
Sequence diagrams must include activation boxes, alt/opt blocks, and return values
Sequence diagrams must show error handling paths
Use case diagrams must show include and extend relationships
Stereotypes (interface, abstract, enum) must be applied appropriately
Large codebases must produce multiple smaller focused diagrams rather than one large diagram
All diagram files must be separate Markdown files with embedded Mermaid code
Color highlighting must be applied using style or CSS class syntax
Source code files must never be modified
Output must be written to analysis_output/uml-generator/

method_breakdown.summary: Creates Mermaid classDiagram visualizing classes, interfaces, enums with attributes/methods and their relationships
parameters: analysis_results (object): From code-documentor with class structures
ast_json (object): From ast-analyzer with detailed class relationships
method_breakdown.returns: Markdown files with embedded Mermaid classDiagram code
method_breakdown.significance: Provides static structure visualization for architecture understanding and documentation

method_breakdown.summary: Creates Mermaid sequenceDiagram for key workflows showing actor interactions, method call chains, and conditional flows
parameters: ast_json (object): Method call chains from ast-analyzer
method_breakdown.returns: Markdown files with embedded Mermaid sequenceDiagram code
method_breakdown.significance: Visualizes dynamic behavior and interaction flows for developer communication and documentation

method_breakdown.summary: Creates Mermaid flowchart-based use case diagrams showing actors, system boundary, use cases, and include/extend relationships
parameters: user_roles (list): Identified actors from code analysis
method_breakdown.returns: Markdown files with embedded Mermaid use case flowchart code
method_breakdown.significance: Documents system functionality from a user perspective for requirements validation
